sentences.text: (BY SRI R.D. RENUKARADHYA, HCGP FOR R1  SRI MANJUNATHA V. RAYAPPA, ADVOCATE FOR R2)

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C PRAYING TO QUASH THE ENTIRE PROCEEDINGS IN C.C.NO. 18859/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE, BENGALURU FOR OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 498A,
323, 504 READ WITH SECTION 34 OF IPC BY ALLOWING THIS PETITION.

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

This petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.2 and 3 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.18859/2019 in Crime No.442/2018 registered by Nandini Layout Police Station, Bengaluru, pending on the file of the VII Addl.
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 read with Section 34 of IPC.

2 . During the pendency of the petition both petitioners and respondent No.2 appeared before the Court along with their counsels and filed joint compromise application on I.A.No.1/2023 under Section 320(2) and 320(8) read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking permission of this Court for compounding the offences.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that accused No.1 who is the mother-in-law of respondent No.2 has already died during the pendency of the proceedings and there is a case filed by the deceased- accused No.1 against respondent No.2 where the petitioners are undertaking to withdraw the said case filed against respondent No.2.
Submission of the petitioners and their counsel is placed on record.

4. In view of settlement between the parties and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2012 CRI.L.J.4934 wherein, it has been held that in cases where the parties have settled the dispute between them,
then, the Court can quash the proceedings.
